transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Reed, Maya Patel, Jordan Kim / Priya Desai, Marcus Holt, Lena Ortiz, Tom Nguyen

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- High-level kickoff for Aurora Springs activation.
- Primary blockers: VPC peering, audit log retention, throughput sizing.
- Redwood to deliver playbook and run initial benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Ethan, AE, with Maya and Jordan from CS and SE. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Priya Desai: Doing well, thanks. Priya here — head of data at Aurora Springs. Marcus and Lena and Tom are here as well.
[00:12] Marcus Holt: Hi all.
[00:13] Lena Ortiz: Hey.
[00:15] Tom Nguyen: Morning. apolog- sorry afternoon, yeah.
[00:18] Ethan: Great. Agenda today — run through activation playbook, map roles for the rollout, confirm security asks (SAML/KMS/audit logs), and set initial benchmark plan. We'll also cover Dedicated vs Hosted options briefly. Sound good?
[00:30] Priya: Yep sounds good. Our timeline: we'd like a pilot by mid April, prod by end of Q2 if everything looks good. Primary constraint is data residency and we want private network, ideally VPC peering or private-link style.
[00:45] Jordan Kim: Ok got it — we typically support VPC peering and customer-managed private deployments; for on-prem there's an air-gap option but that's heavier. For most of our enterprise customers we do a Private deployment where control plane is customer-managed — is that what you had in mind?
[01:02] Marcus: Yes, private control plane. We also need to ensure all traffic stays within our VPC and that we can rotate keys with our KMS.
[01:10] Maya Patel: Noted — on the playbook we'll include the KMS integration steps and where to plug in rotation. There's a sample Terraform module as well.
[01:18] Lena: On compliance — we are SOC 2 in flight, and we need proof that audit logs are retained for 12 months and are exportable. Also SSO is mandatory, SAML 2.0, and we need RBAC scoped to environment.
[01:31] Ethan: Totally. Redwood supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC. For audit logs we can configure retention and ship to your destination via secure forwarder; we'll include the exact fields in the security doc.
[01:41] Tom: When you say "ship" do you mean push or pull? Our security team prefers pull-integration into our SIEM.
[01:47] Jordan: We can do both. There's an agent that pushes to your S3 or we can expose a secure endpoint you poll. We'll note both options.
[01:55] Priya: Excellent. On the performance side — our app sends a mix of short and long contexts; median seq length ~120 tokens but some requests spike to 2k. Cost is a concern so we want to understand batching and quantization recommendations.
[02:10] Jordan: Right — we'll propose two profiles: low-latency (smaller batch / faster kernels) and cost-optimized (larger batching, FP16/8 quantized). There is some tradeoff, for sequences above 1k we recommend model variants with kv cache tuning and continued batching windows.
[02:30] Marcus: Quick question — can Redwood route requests by policy? e.g., critical traffic to Dedicated nodes, cheaper background tasks to hosted pool?
[02:38] Ethan: Yes, smart routing is supported — we can create route policies based on endpoint tags or token tiers. That will be part of the rollout plan.
[02:45] Priya: About benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us to run an initial latency/throughput test?
[02:50] Jordan: A sample request set (JSON lines), preferred sequence length distribution, and baseline SLA target: p50, p95, p99 latencies and QPS we expect. Also whether burst capacity is required.
[03:04] Priya: Ok I'll pull a week's worth of anonymized logs. Is there a preferred format?
[03:09] Jordan: JSONL with fields: prompt, max_tokens, temp, user_id (optional). We'll share a small template.
[03:16] Ethan: Action: Jordan to run bench once they have samples; we'll ingest and produce a spreadsheet with recommended instance sizing and expected unit token cost.
[03:23] Tom: On the Dedicated cost scenarios — do you have an example of reserved capacity pricing vs pay-as-you-go hosted?
[03:28] Maya: Yes, Ethan will send a few modeled scenarios; we typically show committed monthly throughput that gives a lower per-token cost with predictable latency.
[03:36] Marcus: We have an internal procurement window — need contract by April 1 to lock budget for Q2. Is that feasible?
[03:42] Ethan: Feasible. We'll aim to get a draft pricing / term sheet by 2026-03-12.
[03:47] Lena: Security follow-up — can you confirm encryption at rest details and whether keys are customer-managed?
[03:52] Jordan: Yes, KMS integration supported; customer-managed keys are possible for Private deployments. For Hosted we have a managed key by default but also offer Bring-Your-Own Key for enterprise tiers.
[04:03] Priya: Good. One more — do you provide KV cache persistence between restarts? We can't afford cold-start latency on long contexts.
[04:11] Jordan: We persist KV cache to warm nodes for session affinity; however full persistence across infrastructure restarts depends on configuration of Dedicated pools — we'll document expected TTLs and warmup behavior. Sometimes transcription shows this as "KV cash" but it's KV cache.
[04:26] Ethan: Let's walk through the activation playbook quick — step 1: scoping & role signoff, step 2: infra prep (VPC peering, firewall), step 3: connector & secrets (KMS/DB), step 4: smoke tests and benchmarks, step 5: pilot, step 6: rollout.
[04:45] Marcus: For infra prep who owns the peering? Our infra team sets the VPC routes but we need a contact from Redwood to coordinate.
[04:51] Maya: I'll be the primary CS contact and Jordan will handle SE networking. Ethan will manage commercial.
[04:57] Priya: That mapping works. We'll add our infra lead — Diego Ramos — to the VPC deep-dive.
[05:03] Tom: Any known gaps or gotchas we should watch for?
[05:06] Jordan: Firewall egress is common — we require a handful of outbound ports for our control plane. Also watch for MTU sizes if you have transit gateways, that can cause segmentation and higher latency.
[05:17] Lena: On audit — we may need logs to be WORM for legal. Is that supported?
[05:21] Ethan: We can support WORM via S3 object lock when shipping audit logs. We'll confirm in the security doc.
[05:28] Priya: Ok, timeline recap: playbook + pricing by 3/12, sample logs by 3/12, Jordan to bench and share results by 3/15, VPC deep-dive 3/11. Anything else?
[05:38] Tom: Can you also include a runbook for incident escalation and on-call contact? Procurement will want that.
[05:44] Maya: Yes, we'll add a short incident play and contact matrix.
[05:47] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[05:50] Ethan: Great — I'll send notes and attach the activation playbook template.
[05:54] Priya: Thanks, appreciate it. Quick question — any competitor features we should be aware of? I heard about some vector-store caching in other vendors.
[06:01] Jordan: We have prefix caching and KV cache; we also support application-level embedding caches and recommend a hybrid approach. We'll include recommended patterns in the playbook.
[06:11] Marcus: One last ops note — we want to run a small production-like smoke test for 48 hours with synthetic traffic before pilot. Do you support a temporary burst capacity?
[06:20] Ethan: Yes, we can enable burst on Dedicated or provision short-term capacity in Hosted for test windows. We'll outline cost for burst.
[06:28] Priya: Ok that's all from me.
[06:30] Ethan: Excellent. Recap of next steps and owners — Jordan runs benchmarks (SE), Ethan sends pricing & playbook (AE), Maya shares incident runbook and will coordinate the VPC call. Customer to provide logs and infra contact.
[06:44] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:46] Ethan: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the VPC deep-dive and the benchmark handoff.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: some words mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "sock two" for SOC 2), speaker labels intermittently generic.
